main_text.p: nia, mox in India: iam quidem & in Syria, Asiaque. vilissimus autem, & sine ullo nitore in Cappadocia. Probantur qui maxime mellei coloris, in vertice (Cl. Salmasius in vortices) maculosi atque non transluci di. Vitia in iis corneus color aut candidus, & quicquid simile vitro est. Vide quae Cl. Salmasius annotavit ad Solinum pag. 558. & seq.

Plura alia marmora diligenter describit Boetius, ad quae nihil iam addo, praeterquam e Francisco Imperato cap. de marmorum generibus ab Antiquis cognitis, sub finem: Insigne, inquit, marmorum genus silentio praetermittere nolui, a nemine (ni fallor) descriptum, quod ex insula quadam devehitur in Ligustico mari sita, communiter Mons Christi nuncupata, cuius color est albus ad viridem vergens, sed totum est lineis nigris aequidistantibus delineatum; durum equidem genus, raro visitur, ex eo tantum parva fragmenta servamus. page.notes: The woodcut shows a striped, shell-like stone block (marble specimen) with horizontal and diagonal hatching, standing on a ground line. The bottom line of text is partly in italic; the catchword "mar-" is a line-end hyphenated word continuing onto the next page. The caption text at the foot is set in a smaller size. Faint show-through from the reverse page is present and omitted.
